column2: On the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah the Exalted said: O son of Ādam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind.
O son of Ādam, if your sins were to reach the clouds of the sky and you then sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you.

O son of Ādam, if you were to come to Me with sins nearly filling the earth, and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with forgiveness nearly filling it.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Mā daʿawtanī (“as long as you call upon Me”): to forgive your sins; mā is adverbial and verbal (maṣdariyyah ẓarfiyyah).
Wa-rajawtanī (“and hope in Me”): while you hope for My favour upon you and for the answering of your supplication.
Ghafartu laka (“I will forgive you”): your sins; that is, I will cover them for you and not punish you for them in the Hereafter.
“For whatever you have done”: of repeated sins.
Wa-lā ubālī (“and I do not mind”): I am not concerned with your sins nor do I deem them too many, however many they are, for nothing is too great for Me.
ʿAnān (“the clouds”): with fatḥah on the undotted ʿayn; clouds.
Istaghfartanī (“you sought My forgiveness”): you asked Me to protect you from their evil while covering them.
Bi-qurāb al-arḍ (“with nearly filling the earth”): with ḍammah or kasrah on the qāf, ḍammah being better known; that is, with nearly its fill, or with the like of it.
“without associating anything with Me”: because you believe in My oneness and affirm My messengers and what they brought.
The vastness of the generosity and munificence of Allah the Exalted.

A refutation of those who declare Muslims disbelievers on account of sins, and of the Muʿtazilah, who hold the position of “a station between the two stations”, meaning that [the sinner] is neither a believer nor a disbeliever in this world and will abide forever in the Fire in the Hereafter.

The correct view is that of Ahl al-Sunnah: the name of faith is not stripped from the sinner, nor is it given to him without qualification; rather, it is said that he is a sinful believer, or a believer by his faith and a transgressor by his major sin. This is what the Book, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Salaf of the nation indicate.
An explanation of the meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh: it is singling out Allah in worship and leaving shirk, little and much.

Forgiveness is attained through these three causes: supplication with hope, seeking forgiveness, and tawḥīd, which is the greatest cause; whoever lacks it has lost forgiveness, and whoever brings it has brought the greatest cause of forgiveness.
The printed text reads الذي فقه فقد المغفرة, evidently for الذي من فقده فقد المغفرة (“whoever lacks it has lost forgiveness”).
